analysis.title: If The Spenders And The Receivers Are Both Getting Crushed, Who's Left To Pay The AI Bill?
key_insights: Demand for AI is not in question: Google Cloud doubled, Azure grew 48%, AWS grew 39% (fastest in five years, highest operating margin ever). Stocks fell anyway as investors shifted to wanting returns and cash flow over capex.
Tech has shed about $5 trillion of market cap over three weeks. The Nasdaq fell 5% last week, the SOX fell 7% on Friday, and on Monday the NDX took out Friday's lows and entered a correction.

Alphabet missed on revenue and EPS and reported negative free cash flow, its worst stock move in 20 years, erasing $500 billion of market cap in a day. Amazon's trailing 12-month FCF turned negative with higher capex signaled for next year. Intel had its largest one-day drop on record on a weak Q4 guide and a cash burn warning for FY26.
The SOX closed below its 200-day moving average for the first time in a year. Semis trade at roughly 16x forward earnings, back at AI-cycle lows.

Per Molavi, the big 4 hyperscalers' combined FCF is $26bn, and they are financing increasingly with debt and equity (Meta raise last week). Amazon long-term debt rose from $66bn to $173bn in 9 months.

GS chart: hyperscaler capex as a share of operating cash flow was about 40% in 2024, is above 80% now, and is heading to roughly 105% in 2026 and 112% in 2027 on consensus. The only precedent is S&P 500 Telecom in 2000. Hyperscaler FCF goes from about $240bn in 2024 to about negative $140bn in 2027 (read off the chart, approximate).

GS TMT desk: negative FCF at Google, Amazon and Meta plus more than $3tn of forward commitments shifts focus to funding duration. Microsoft is self-funding but just issued $25bn of debt. Hyperscaler CDS at records, Oracle CDS near 288bp, S&P negative outlook on Meta (AA- maintained). Credit stress could ultimately force a capex pause.

Borrowing continued Monday: Oracle plans another $20bn of bond and stock sales, and Alphabet is selling €6bn of euro bonds. Meta's 5Y CDS is 60bps wider this year, wider than ratings and fundamentals imply per GS credit exotics desk, which is packaging hyperscaler CDS into structured notes.

Molavi is puzzled that spenders and receivers of AI capex are falling together. The article's answer is circular financing: when the spender pays with borrowed money, the receiver's revenue depends on the spender's credit. Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom indicated interest in buying part of Meta's stock offering (per FT via GS TMT desk), which weakens the offtake narrative supporting Oracle.

GS AI basket has fallen from about 155 at its late-spring peak to below 120, while the S&P 500 ex-AI just hit new highs. Molavi calls it a 'stealth bear market': the S&P is 3% from its high, the Mag 7 lost $4 trillion since Oct 15, and 60% of S&P members are in bear market territory.

Drawdowns from all-time highs per Molavi: Applovin -65%, Western Digital -52%, Oracle -50%, Arm -49%, ServiceNow -37%, Intel -35%, Broadcom -31%, Marvell -30%, Alphabet -28%, Meta -22%. On the day Alphabet lost $500bn the S&P fell only 30bps as healthcare, real estate and staples outperformed.

Credit signal: the B vs CCC spread hit 8% only 5 times since 1996, and each time the S&P was at least 11.5% below its 52-week high (about 30% twice). The S&P was less than 2% below the high coming into last week.

Gross was extremely hard to carry for a third straight week, and the key spreads (software vs semis, value vs growth, small vs big, cyclicals vs defensives) were very difficult to manage. TMT funds lost 11.9% in October. The cyclicals-vs-defensives gauge is down 13% in this episode, worse than Liberation Day's -12%.

Not all of GS is bearish on funding: the bank's software analyst says financing needed may be less than investors expect and the market is deep enough for IG issuers. Nadella said bigger training budgets must be funded by real revenues and faster growth.

Upcoming catalysts: more Mag 7 earnings, next steps on Iran, and Tuesday's midterms, where market-implied odds of a Democratic sweep rose to 72%, up 7 points in two days. Molavi's backdrop is high rates, falling equities, $100+ oil, geopolitical uncertainty, political tail risks and rising CPI, PPI and PCE inflation.
The article sides with credit: it expects the next capex revision to be higher and the next bond deal bigger, and sees the stealth bear market's only remaining place to go as the index.

market_movers.rationale: Missed on revenue and EPS with negative FCF. Worst move in 20 years, $500bn of market cap lost in a day, -28% from the all-time high.

sector_views.rationale: SOX below its 200-day average for the first time in a year, about 16x forward earnings, and Intel's record drop. Molavi says chip demand remains rock solid.
They outperformed on the day Alphabet lost $500bn, and staples have had a large surge.

earnings_insights: Alphabet reported (week of 10/26-10/30): revenue and EPS missed, free cash flow negative. Figures are not given in the note.
Amazon reported: AWS grew 39%, its fastest pace in five years, at its highest operating margin ever. Trailing 12-month FCF turned negative and management signaled higher capex next year.
Intel reported: Q4 guide weak and cash burn warning for FY26, largest one-day drop on record.
Google Cloud revenue doubled and Azure grew 48% in the latest reported quarter.

macro_indicators.indicator: Market-implied odds of a Democratic sweep in midterms
macro_indicators.interpretation: Up 7 points in two days. Midterm years tend to be volatile into the vote and kinder afterward.
Part of Molavi's backdrop of high rates, falling equities and rising CPI, PPI and PCE inflation.

trade_ideas.description: Buy hyperscaler bonds (Hartnett flipped from shorting them, his best trade into 2026, to buying them)
trade_ideas.rationale: Hartnett frames the bond market as policing the AI capex boom.

tension_points.bull_case: The GS software analyst says financing needed may be less than investors expect and the IG market is deep enough. Demand is solid, with AWS +39%, Azure +48% and Google Cloud doubling.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex above 100% of operating cash flow, negative FCF at Google, Amazon and Meta, record CDS and rising debt issuance, with only S&P Telecom in 2000 as a precedent.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscalers cannot deliver positive cash flow until 2028 at the earliest on consensus, and the next capex revision comes in higher.

tension_points.theme: stealth bear market vs credit signal
tension_points.bull_case: The S&P is only 3% from its all-time high and midterm years tend to be kinder after the vote.
tension_points.bear_case: The B vs CCC spread hit 8% five times since 1996, and each time the S&P was at least 11.5% below its high.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Credit spreads tightening, or equities falling at least 11.5% from the high to match prior episodes.
